page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance built on x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server provides 32 vCPUs split across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and BMI2 flags. Virtualized on a KVM hypervisor, the instance includes 15 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth but provides no local NVMe or SSD storage drives.

Performance evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core scalability alongside weaker single-core processing metrics. Multi-threaded benchmark scores—including stress-ng multi-core (23,406.46), Geekbench multi-core (8,312.0), and PassMark CPU (23,344.34)—place in the average range for its class. In application tests, the instance records 23.48 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 14.04 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded throughput is restricted, as seen in weak stress-ng single-core (1,106.88) and single-core Geekbench (951.0) scores, along with low single-threaded gzip compression speed (19.05 GB/sec). Large block memory read bandwidth reaches 119.7 GB/sec, supporting standard memory access patterns under heavy load.

From a hardware efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5ne.8xlarge yields balanced resource allocation, trading single-core execution speed for parallel processing density across 32 virtual cores. The absence of local disk storage requires reliance on network-attached storage solutions, which should be factored into architectural designs. This instance profile is effective for general-purpose workloads capable of multi-threaded parallelization, including static and dynamic web server clusters, middle-tier enterprise application services, Redis caching systems, software compilation, and small to medium model LLM inference prompt processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance equipped with 32 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, configured at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processors using the x86_64 architecture, it features 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled and support for AVX-512 extensions. Running on KVM virtualization, this instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps and contains no local storage. Benchmark results show average multi-core CPU capacity and solid memory bandwidth, achieving 23.48 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.04 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, single-core CPU speeds and single-threaded compression performance remain weak. This instance offers reasonable cost efficiency for resource-dense multi-core workloads, making it well-suited for web serving, software compilation with Clang, medium-scale database operations, and multi-threaded web application backends.
